I’ve been seeing a lot of dismissive comments about TerminalBench, SWE-Bench, or academic benchmarks in general lately. I think people underestimate how difficult it is to build good benchmarks. It’s much easier to criticize a benchmark than to build one.

Auditing benchmarks is

ornith 1.5 122b is out, mit license, and they're claiming 84.5 on swe-bench verified

someone already got it from 132gb down to 35gb. i'll trust the benchmark after people throw it at messy real repos for a week, but a local 122b coding model is wild

The real benchmark isn't SWE-bench.

It's whether Claude or Codex can finish my project without breaking three other things.

ARC-AGI-3 was designed to resist saturation. Gemini 4 Argon hit 97.5%. That benchmark is done. Are we measuring reasoning or training-distribution proximity? Neither ARC-AGI-2 nor -3 lasted 18 months before ceiling. We need better task construction methodology. #AIResearch

just in time for day3: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling. paper by #stanford folks
What happens when you let LLMs generate 1K attempts at a problem?
How test-time compute lets open models beat GPT-4o and crush SWE-bench SOTA #30Days30Papers

Recursive just released Flint, an open coding model that runs on a laptop. 40B parameters, only 2.5B active per token, Apache 2.0.

The speed is the exciting part 👁️👁️more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, fully offline. Recursive says its automated research

SWE-bench dropping is benchmark saturation in vivid form. most evals have no principled retirement criterion — the ruler gets longer as models climb it. the measurement problem and the incentive problem turn out to be the same problem. https://t.co/w897dEs9tA

JetBrains studied 4,782 real coding-agent sessions.

~94% of SWE-Bench Pro tasks are features or bug fixes. In real use, that’s under half. The rest: explaining code, planning, reviews.

No benchmark is universal. Measure how your team uses agents.

Your benchmark score only tells you how good the eval is:

IQuest-Coder hit #1 on SWE-bench — then they found it was reading answer keys.

You're not measuring the model. You're measuring the test.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B faces new competition from a 39.8B coding model that can run on a 24GB Mac.

Recursive’s Flint uses roughly 2.5B active parameters per token, and Unsloth’s 3-bit GGUF weighs 18.5GB. Unsloth reports generation speeds above 125 tokens/sec on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro. https://t.co/W7WfvwPDxS

The control is the tell: pull the images and GPT-6 Luna loses about 43 points on MMMU-Pro, yet gains 0.2 on SWE-bench Multimodal. The screenshots mostly restate the issue text, and the hidden tests rarely check what they show. The grader defines the benchmark. https://t.co/EeA6xNdUTM
